title: Preliminary U.S. Imports for Consumption of Steel Products (Census, Aug 2026 data) — the metals-input read the morning before durable goods
source: CENSUS: two independent census.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-08 by this event's own initial research. (1) economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes, 179 rows parsed) carries 'Preliminary U.S. Imports for Consumption of Steel Products | September 24, 2026 | 10:00 AM | August 2026', slot A202609241000, reference period A202608. (2) The CURRENT EDITION'S OWN RELEASE, foreign-trade/Press-Release/steel/steelp_2607.pdf (HTTP 200, 657,331 bytes; Release Number CB26-137, FT-900A (26-07), 'FOR RELEASE AT 10:00 AM EDT, THURSDAY, AUGUST 27, 2026'), states verbatim: 'The August report is scheduled for release on September 24, 2026.' Third check, mechanical and independent of the grid: every prior edition's own 'next report' sentence chains to the following grid row without a break across 2023-2026. Flipped estimate -> confirmed by this event's own initial research, which is exactly the condition the no-self-confirm limit names (the same promotion durable-goods-2026-09-25 made off primary (1)); CENSUS: is the authorized confirmed-tier prefix for a census.gov schedule
notes: NEVER TRADE THE 10:00 MINUTE; READ THE YEAR-TO-DATE LINE, NOT THE MONTH; AND TRUST THE AGGREGATE, NOT THE COUNTRY SPLITS. The tape effect is MEASURED, not assumed: across 39 realized releases (2023-01-26 -> 2026-08-27, dates parsed from Census's own four calendar-year grids), NUE's open->close move net of XLB averages +0.264% (t=+1.16, p=0.25) — and the residual drift dies against a calendar control, because the same day-of-month 23-28 non-release sessions average +0.197% (release-vs-control t=+0.26, p=0.79). Dropping the 7 release days inside a +/-1d steel-earnings window leaves n=32 with a mean absolute abnormal move of 0.97% against 1.00% on ordinary non-earnings days and a variance ratio of 0.80 — this print's sessions are QUIETER than average, and the tail base rate is flat (|abnormal| > 1.5% on 22% of release days vs 22% of ordinary days). symbols: [] is therefore kept deliberately, though NUE sits in this app's own ticker directory. AND 10:00 ET ON 09-24 IS THE MOST CONTAMINATED MINUTE ON THE CALENDAR: new-home-sales-2026-09-24 publishes at the same hour on the same August reference month with a published consensus this release does not have, and the estimate-dated trump-xi-summit-2026-09-24 owns the day's tariff narrative, which is what actually prices steel. THE SUSPENSION RECORD IS FIVE MONTHS, NOT TWO, AND THE DATA WAS NOT LOST. The 2025 grid adds three suspended slots to the 2026 grid's two: reference months Sep-2025, Oct-2025, Nov-2025, Dec-2025 and Jan-2026 all read 'Suspended', with no make-up slot; the last pre-lapse edition is August-2025 data on 2025-09-24 and the series resumes with February-2026 data on 2026-03-25. Mechanically confirmed: steelp_2509 through steelp_2601.pdf all return HTTP 404 — while steelf_2509 through steelf_2601.pdf, the FINAL FT-900A steel reports for the same months, all return HTTP 200. Census killed the EARLY READ and kept the NUMBER, so what a lapse costs this series is the ~4-week head start, not the data — which corrects both durable-goods-2026-09-25's 'Census delayed, never deleted' generalization and this event's own founding proposal, and calibrates the 2026-12-22 edition, the one sitting 11 days past the CR's 2026-12-11 expiry. THE CONTENT IS A SLOW STRUCTURAL GAUGE AND IT IS SAYING SOMETHING: the July edition put YTD final imports through June 2026 at 10.3 Mmt against 13.3 Mmt in 2025 (-22.6%), while FRED primaries show PPI iron and steel +17.6% y/y (318.1 -> 374.1) on essentially flat domestic output (IPG331S +1.6%). Researched in docs/research/events/steel-imports-preliminary-2026-09-24.md; canonical file written by that research from the one existing proposal (from-durable-goods-2026-09-25), which it shadows.
